reading.body:
CyrusOne's Council Bluffs OCB1 publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, half of Iowa's declared 18 MW and far too small to be a hyperscale AI training site.

The pattern is that disclosed data center capacity is rare. Iowa has 52 mapped data center sites, and only two of them publish power figures, which together total 18 MW. OCB1 is one of those two. Its 420,000 square feet of technical space against 9 MW implies a low power density by AI standards. At the 40 kW per rack density typical of AI training, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks, or under 100 accelerators once four GPUs per rack and non-compute overhead are accounted for. That is a multi-hall regional campus, not a dense training cluster.

For AI specifically, the certifications matter more than the capacity. PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, HITRUST, and TIA-942 describe a building designed for regulated enterprise and government workloads, which prioritize compliance and redundancy over maximum power per square foot. AI scaling is limited by power and by buildings, and this building has far more floor space than power. The suitability score of 56, derived from published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing, is consistent with that reading.

What the data does not cover is who occupies the campus, whether the 9 MW is fully contracted, or whether additional power is available at the site. Because most Iowa sites publish no power specification, the state's 18 MW figure is a floor on disclosed capacity rather than a measure of actual load. No address, airport, or expansion data is given, so nothing here establishes this facility as a node in a larger AI buildout.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
